title: You committed three times to main by mistake
summary: Feature work landed on main instead of a branch. Move it to where it belongs and put main back, without losing a line — the single most common git accident there is.
mental_model: The commits are fine — only the branch pointer is wrong. Create a branch here (naming the work), then move main back to where it should be. Two pointer moves, no content touched.

steps.title: Confirm the damage — and that it is local
steps.why: Three commits ahead of origin/main. Nothing has been pushed, which means this is a pointer problem and not a history-rewrite problem. Check this before anything else: if they were pushed, the answer would be revert instead.
steps.expect: ahead 3, and the three feature commits listed.

verify.label: three unpushed commits sit on main

steps.title: Name the work before moving anything
steps.why: `git branch feature/dosing` creates a branch at your current position without moving you. The commits now have a second name — so whatever happens to main next, they are safe.
steps.expect: Both main and feature/dosing point at the same commit.

verify.label: the branch holds all the work

steps.title: Move main back to where the server has it
steps.why: `reset --hard origin/main` moves main's pointer back three commits and matches the working tree to it. The commits are not deleted — feature/dosing still points at them, which is why step 2 came first.
steps.expect: main is in sync with origin, and the dosing files are gone from the working tree.

verify.label: main is back to the released state

steps.title: Continue on the branch where you meant to be
steps.why: Switch to the feature branch and the files are back. Nothing was recreated — you simply moved to the pointer that still names those commits.

verify.label: the work is intact on its own branch

steps.title: The variant: copying commits somewhere else instead
steps.why: When the commits belong on a branch that already exists, cherry-pick a range onto it. `A..B` works here exactly as it does in log — but the range must start where the target branch already agrees, or you get modify/delete conflicts from commits that edit files the target has never seen.
steps.expect: All three commits copied across with new shas. Starting the range at feature/dosing~2 instead would conflict, because that skips the commit that creates dosing.py.

verify.label: a commit range was cherry-picked onto another branch

steps.title: Know the escape hatch
steps.why: Had you run the reset *before* creating the branch, the reflog would still have the commits — `git reset --hard HEAD@{1}` or `git branch rescue <sha>` gets them back. The branch-first order just means you never have to.

steps.title: Prevent the next one
steps.why: Most people who do this once do it weekly. A `main` branch that refuses direct commits — via a pre-commit hook locally or branch protection on the server — turns the accident into an error message.
steps.expect: Nothing to run here; the fix is a hook or server-side protection.

verify.label: main is back to the released state
verify.hint: branch first, then git reset --hard origin/main

verify.label: the misplaced work lives on a feature branch
main is in sync with origin again
you also copied a commit range with cherry-pick
verify.hint: git cherry-pick main..feature/dosing — start the range where the target agrees

pitfalls: Create the branch BEFORE resetting. Doing it the other way round works only because of the reflog, and only for 90 days.
`git reset --hard` discards uncommitted changes too. Stash them first if you have any.
If the commits were already pushed to a shared main, this whole approach is wrong — use `git revert` instead, or you force-push over other people.
A cherry-pick range that starts mid-feature drops the commits that created the files, producing modify/delete conflicts. Start at the branch point.
`git switch -c <branch>` moves you as well as creating the branch. Plain `git branch <name>` leaves you where you are, which is what you want mid-rescue.
cheatsheet: name the current commit without moving
put main back to the server's state
continue where you meant to be
copy a range of commits onto another branch
the net, if you reset before branching
